doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Army band in Colorado Springs with Tommy Turk
summary: He played piano in trombonist Tommy Turk's band at officers' clubs and came home in a zoot suit, now a musician.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: It might be a good idea to agree here... I’m just joking. So you were in Fort McClellan. Then you go to Colorado Springs, and you play in the Army band there. I gather you were associated with the trombonist Tommy Turk, who later would play with Charlie Parker.

Yes. Tommy Turk was a great trombonist, and I used to play with him... I was playing piano in his band, and we used to play at officers’ clubs and around. He was a great player. I knew it at the time, but I later met him when he was with Jazz at the Philharmonic...

I think the Army really changed you a lot, probably, because of music. Your mother has a famous story that when they went to meet you at the train you were dressed in a zoot suit, and that’s not how she sent you off.
So at some point between 1943 or so, when you’re in high school, and by the time you’re discharged from the Army at 20 or 19, you’re a musician.
You’re not going to be a chemical engineer any more.
Yeah. I took mechanical drawing, and I did well in chemistry, but...
He was a good painter and drawing.
So you had a kinesthetic skill.
